page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn7i-4x.16xlarge is a dedicated GPU-accelerated server configuration operating under the KVM hypervisor. The host system provides 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8369B processors clocked at a base frequency of 2.9 GHz. It features 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an even resource distribution of 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU.

Hardware acceleration is delivered by four NVIDIA A10 GPUs providing a total of 96 GB of GDDR6 VRAM, configured as 24 GB per accelerator. For high-volume data exchange, the instance is equipped with a 64 Gbps baseline network interface. Local storage is not bundled with this configuration, meaning all system disks and application data volumes must be provisioned via remote block storage. Zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

The dense four-GPU architecture offers substantial parallel execution capacity without the extreme cost footprint of specialized deep learning training clusters. Workloads well matched to this infrastructure profile include multi-stream machine learning inference, computer vision processing, video encoding and transcoding, virtual workstation rendering, and distributed visual computing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn7i-4x.16xlarge is a dedicated GPU-accelerated instance designed for high-throughput compute and parallel rendering tasks. It is equipped with 64 x86_64 vCPUs running on 2.9 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processors and 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Acceleration is handled by four NVIDIA A10 GPUs offering a cumulative 96 GB of VRAM, with 24 GB allocated per accelerator. The system features a 64 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface to facilitate high-speed data transfer across cloud environments. Because local physical storage is not bundled with the instance, persistent data and root volumes require attached cloud storage volumes. With four discrete GPUs and dedicated host resources, the ecs.gn7i-4x.16xlarge is structured for multi-stream AI inference, cloud graphics rendering, computer vision, and video transcoding workloads requiring significant graphics memory and high network throughput.
